$comment: SHIPPED, deliberately. The reference implementation this plugin succeeds is FROZEN at v0.11.3 and ships no gates file of its own -- neither nen/gates.json nor the legacy schemas/gates.json -- because CON-32's reviewer identities lived as a literal in its own gate predicates, not as data. `nen pr ready` never falls back to a built-in reviewer set (a binary that guessed would judge a repository against another one's vocabulary and could report a false ready), so judging a PR in that frozen repository requires --gates pointed at a file carrying those same identities. This is that file: a copy, taken at nen v0.1.0, of nen's own shadow-window-validated reviewer-identity fixture (zheref/nen, then at src/schema/fixtures/bankai-repo/schemas/gates.json; since nen v0.3.0 that fixture lives at src/schema/fixtures/bankai-repo/nen/gates.json -- the canonical taxonomy directory is now nen/, and schemas/ is a read-only fallback removed in v0.4.0), which nen's docs/evidence/shadow-window-p1.md proved byte-for-byte parity against scripts/pr_ready_gate.sh's hard-coded identities across the live estate (16/16, then 17/17 agreement runs). Carried here, in hatsu, as the pr-state skill's --gates argument for that reference repository specifically -- see claude/skills/pr-state/SKILL.md. Always pass it as an ABSOLUTE path -- $hatsu_root/contracts/reference.gates.json, $hatsu_root being the Hatsu checkout as claude/skills/hatsu-warmup/SKILL.md section 5's prelude resolves and canonicalises it, in the shell that runs the call, on every surface; $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT alone is Claude Code's and is unset or wrong on Codex and Cursor: since nen v0.2.0 a RELATIVE --gates resolves against --repo, not the cwd, and --gates never falls back to either taxonomy location. A repo that ships its own nen/gates.json (or, until v0.4.0, schemas/gates.json) needs no --gates flag at all; this file exists only because the reference implementation, being frozen, cannot grow one.

reviewers.$comment: Posts as copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]; nothing re-requests it after a final push, so under the bounded policy only a PENDING request owes a round.
reviewers.name: copilot

reviewers.$comment: The check IS the round: it posts a review only when it has findings. The enrolment pattern is ANCHORED and CASE-SENSITIVE on purpose -- a sibling probe job would otherwise enrol the reviewer on every PR. It is not a DEFAULT approver, but it joins the approval set for a PR it has actually posted a review on at head -- the shell's `approvers="$approvers,bisky"` arm.
reviewers.name: bisky

reviewers.$comment: Posts under a login carrying either word depending on the installation, and its check name varies with the installation too -- hence an UNANCHORED, case-insensitive substring where bisky's is anchored.
reviewers.name: bugbot
